correctness.rationale: The original five-coordinate bracket, center, and derived algebra are verified from the cited source. Over every odd characteristic, its three commutator coordinates are an invertible linear transform of the three 2x2 minors in K^3. This proves the centralizer-line partition and Gaussian A_d formula for all m,q. If an abelian ideal contains an element with a or b nonzero, choosing v with ay-bx nonzero forces [u,[u,v]] nonzero, a contradiction. Otherwise it lies in L'; the presence of nonzero c forces Z, proving exact J_d. Complete RREF finite-field enumerations over F_3 and F_5 verify both counts, full centralizers over F_3 and K=F_9 proportionality provide additional checks; these do not substitute for proof. All quantifiers, zero dimensions, and odd-characteristic boundary are explicit.

originality.rationale: The primary 2022 full text provides the algebra and, in Proposition 3.2, essentially the centralizer minor constraints; those are expressly treated as known. What is not supplied there is the all-dimensional Gaussian-binomial census of abelian subalgebras and ideals, nor the classification of all abelian ideals. The finite-field subspace partition and ideal-rigidity proof supply the additional facts. The 2025 graph treatment gives general abelian-cover relationships without these per-dimension distributions. Low-dimensional classification tables may contain isolated m=1 qualitative facts. Published public mathematical research index comparisons matched no claimed stronger implication, and the remaining terminological/history risks are disclosed.

value.rationale: For the natural unique stem family of all class-three nilpotent Lie algebras of breadth type (0,2m), the result completely enumerates two structural invariants by dimension for every odd finite field and extension degree. The projective-plane incidence family of Q^2+Q+1 maximal abelian subalgebras versus one maximal abelian ideal and explicit uniform Gaussian censuses provide interpretable information for representation of subalgebra lattices, distinct from mere centralizer breadth or low-dimensional isomorphism lists. It is a complete motivated classification rather than a small numerical increment.
